cards.anchor: Whole-load rack fit and charge limits coexist with nine source unloads, twelve releases, and B9 correction; batch capacity alone does not establish lower labor.
cards.burden: Transfer clerk works seven minutes and uses both trolley allowances; inspection clerk works thirteen minutes. The clerk must switch vehicles at boundary 1 and maintain the specified load order.
cards.construction: Hand carry B4 during 0-1; trolley B5-B8 during 1-4; trolley B9-B12 during 4-7. Inspect B1-B8 consecutively during 0-8, correct and seal B9 during 8-10, then inspect B10-B12 during 10-13. Completion before unloading leaves zero rack carriers at 4 and one at 7, so both four-carrier loads fit.
cards.defeat: Reject if the boundary ledger shows any blocked unload, transfer occupation above seven minutes, or fewer than twelve physically correct completed seals by 13. Equal final performance supplies no evidence of superiority over the rival.
cards.mutation: Move the single hand-carried remainder to the first trip, making the second trolley load contain B9 through B12.
cards.prediction_candidate: Finite-model prediction: one source carrier unloaded by 1, five by 4, nine by 7; twelve correct releases by 13, including corrected B9, with seven occupied transfer minutes and no blocked unloading.
cards.prediction_rival: Finite-model prediction: zero source unloads by 1, four by 3, eight by 6, nine by 7; the same twelve correct releases and seven occupied transfer minutes.
cards.probe: Replay both schedules against the stated boundary rules; ledger carrier identities, whole-load fit, charge use, occupied intervals, physical bracket counts and completed seals. Boundary-1 source unload counts distinguish the schedules; final counts test feasibility and the predicted tie.
cards.rival: Full-load-first archive operation: trolley B4-B7 during 0-3, trolley B8-B11 during 3-6, then hand carry B12 during 6-7, with continuous ordered inspection.
unknowns: Later request adaptation remains unobserved and does not change this window.
These are calculated schedules, not trial outcomes, empirical distributions or a global optimality proof.
